`receive` makes 2 domain intake calls. A webhook hands the verified delivery to exactly one domain method that records its inbox delivery in a transaction; a separate first domain proof is allowed, and a second intake is orchestration that belongs in that method.

`receive` makes a second delegating call here. A thin file makes exactly one; a second is orchestration - step order, compensation, claim, fencing, retry - and belongs to a capability of the platform or inside the service the file calls.

`receive` makes 2 domain intake calls. A webhook hands the verified delivery to exactly one domain method that records its inbox delivery in a transaction; a separate first domain proof is allowed, and a second intake is orchestration that belongs in that method.

[BE_WEBHOOK_SCOPE] The domain intake this webhook door calls processes the delivery inside its receipt transaction: a `process` callback, a call to the command or query bus, or a call to a domain service that is not a receipt port. The receipt transaction only records the inbox delivery (the platform Inbox, or a domain receipt port whose constructor takes only platform ports, one of them the Inbox) and publishes the typed outbox event; a reactor or job processes the delivery after commit.
